mainTopic: Paying a בכור examiner, and what one may buy from people suspected about בכורות, שביעית, and תרומה
overview: The amud first finishes the earlier משנה about paying a כהן examiner. It gives two ways he could become טמא: a trodden בית הפרס, whose טומאה is only מדרבנן, or other kinds of טומאה a כהן may contract that still stop him from eating תרומה. An elderly examiner who must ride a donkey is paid like an idle worker, and אביי explains that this means idle from his own particular job. Then a new משנה lists what one may not buy from someone suspected about בכור animals: not even deer meat, untanned hides, or raw wool. Spun thread and garments are allowed, and רבי אליעזר also allows female hides. The גמרא explains each rule, including the argument over whether a seller could fake a female hide by blaming mice. It also shows that the 'extra' words in the משנה mean wool cleaned of its dirt, and felt. Two more משניות follow. One covers a person suspected about שביעית, where 'woven' means braided chains. The other covers a person suspected of selling תרומה as חולין, where רבי שמעון's wording includes fish innards mixed with olive oil. A story about a suspected butcher begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A trodden field of graves is pure
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה בר אמי, quoting רב יהודה, rules that a בית הפרס that people have walked over until it became a path is pure.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה בר אמי said in the name of רב יהודה: a בית הפרס that has been trodden down is pure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is explaining how a כהן examiner could get טמא in the משנה's case. It brings a ruling that a well-trodden בית הפרס is pure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The טומאה of a בית הפרס is only מדרבנן, so it is fairly easy for it to become pure, for example once people tread a path through it. This shows a כהן might walk there. Even so, he may still not eat תרומה until he purifies himself, so the person who brought him there owes him for that loss.

keyTerms.meaning: A field where a grave was plowed up, so small bones may be scattered in it
Trodden down, flattened by people walking over it

phrases.aramaic: וְרַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר:
phrases.english: And Rav Yehuda bar Ami said in the name of Rav Yehuda:
A beit haperas that has been trodden down is pure.
phrases.notes: Once people have walked a path through it, we stop worrying about bones there.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַב יְהוּדָה בַּר אַמֵּי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier answer (from before this section) that the כהן became טמא through a בית הפרס.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A trodden בית הפרס is pure, because its טומאה is only מדרבנן.

steps.title: Or he became impure through other kinds of impurity
steps.stepSummary: A second answer: the כהן became טמא through other kinds of טומאה, which a כהן is not forbidden to contract.
steps.simpleTranslation: Alternatively: the case is about other kinds of טומאה, which a כהן is not warned against.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer to the same question of how the כהן became טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כהן is only forbidden to become טמא from a dead body. Other kinds of טומאה are allowed for him, but they still stop him from eating תרומה. So the משנה can be talking about one of those other kinds of טומאה.

keyTerms.meaning: Other kinds of impurity (not from a dead body)
Warned, commanded not to do something

steps.whatToRemember: There are two ways the כהן examiner could become טמא: a בית הפרס (only מדרבנן), or other kinds of טומאה that a כהן is allowed to contract. Either way he loses the chance to eat תרומה, and he must be paid for that loss.

phrases.english: Alternatively:
it is with other impurities,
which he is not warned against.
phrases.notes: He means the כהן: he is only forbidden to become טמא from a dead body.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer instead of the בית הפרס answer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think a כהן could never become טמא in the course of this job, because he is forbidden to.
steps.terutzMaskana: He can become טמא through allowed kinds of טומאה, which still keep him from eating תרומה.

steps.title: An elderly examiner is paid like an idle worker
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of an elderly person who must be put on a donkey, and a ברייתא says he is paid like an idle worker.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: if he was elderly, the owner puts him on a donkey. A ברייתא taught: he is paid like an idle worker.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves on to the next line of the משנה and brings a ברייתא that explains how much the elderly person is paid. This sets up אביי's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Taking pay for judging or examining is normally forbidden. But since he lost a day of his own work, he may get paid for that loss. The ברייתא calls this being paid 'like an idle worker', and it does not yet explain what that means.

keyTerms.meaning: An idle worker, someone kept from his usual work

phrases.english: If he was elderly —
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה, about the examiner, judge or witness.

phrases.english: he puts him to ride on the donkey.
It was taught: like an idle worker.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם הָיָה זָקֵן מַרְכִּיבוֹ עַל הַחֲמוֹר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of טומאה and turns to the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The payment is like that of an idle worker.

steps.title: אביי: idle from his own particular work
steps.stepSummary: אביי explains that 'idle worker' means a worker kept from his own specific job.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: like a worker who is idle from that particular job of his.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains exactly what the ברייתא's phrase 'like an idle worker' means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The pay is not a fixed amount and not his full wage. It is the amount a person in his line of work would accept to give up that work for the day and do this task instead. So it depends on how hard his own job is and how much it pays.

keyTerms.meaning: That particular work, his own usual job

steps.whatToRemember: An elderly examiner who loses a day of work is paid for that loss, measured by his own job: the amount someone would accept to stop doing that job and do this one.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not his full salary. It is the smaller amount a person would accept to sit out from his own kind of work.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
like a worker idle from that particular work.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the phrase from the ברייתא in step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What exactly does 'like an idle worker' mean?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It means a worker kept idle from his own specific kind of work, paid accordingly.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Idle worker' means a worker kept idle from his own particular kind of work, and he is paid accordingly.

steps.title: New משנה: what not to buy from a suspect
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that from a person suspected of selling בכור meat, one may not buy even deer meat, and not untanned hides.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: From one suspected about firstborn animals, one may not buy deer meat, nor hides that are not tanned.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists items one may not buy from a person suspected of selling forbidden בכור meat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suspect is someone suspected of illicitly making a blemish in a בכור, or of selling the meat of an unblemished בכור as ordinary meat. A בכור that was inspected and found blemished may be slaughtered, and its meat eaten and sold, with some market limits. The fear is that he passes off forbidden בכור meat as permitted. So the משנה forbids even deer meat from him, since he could sell a בכור calf and call it deer, and also untanned hides, since a hide could come from an unblemished בכור.

keyTerms.meaning: The משנה (start of a new משנה)

phrases.english: Mishnah:
One who is suspected regarding firstborn animals,
phrases.notes: Suspected of slaughtering and selling בכור animals when it is forbidden.

phrases.english: one may not buy deer meat from him,
nor hides that are not tanned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה on a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From a suspect, one may not buy even deer meat or untanned hides.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר allows hides of female animals
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר says one may buy hides of female animals from the suspect.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: one may buy hides of female animals from him.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אליעזר adds a leniency to the hides rule: female hides are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The laws of בכור apply only to males. So a hide that is clearly from a female cannot be a בכור hide, and there is nothing to worry about.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
one may buy hides of a female animal from him,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the ban on untanned hides from step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hides of female animals may be bought from the suspect.

steps.title: Raw wool is forbidden, spun thread and garments are allowed
steps.stepSummary: The משנה forbids buying bleached or dirty wool from the suspect, but allows spun thread and garments.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one may not buy bleached or dirty wool from him, but one may buy spun thread and garments from him.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes on to wool. Raw wool is forbidden to buy from the suspect, while wool that has already been spun or made into clothing is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wool of a בכור is forbidden. Wool that is still raw, whether bleached or dirty, could be from a בכור. Once it has been spun into thread or woven into garments, the משנה permits buying it.
steps.whatToRemember: From a suspect: no meat (not even deer), no untanned hides, and no raw wool. But tanned hides, female hides (according to רבי אליעזר), spun thread and garments are allowed.

phrases.english: And one may not buy from him
bleached wool or dirty wool,
but one may buy spun thread and garments from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין לוֹקְחִין מִמֶּנּוּ צֶמֶר מְלוּבָּן וְצוֹאִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from hides to wool, listing what is forbidden and what is allowed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Raw wool is forbidden to buy from the suspect; spun thread and garments are allowed.

steps.title: Why deer meat is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that deer meat is forbidden from the suspect because it can be confused with calf meat.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Deer meat? Because it can be confused with calf meat.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting the משנה's surprising rule about deer meat and gives the reason for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Deer meat has no בכור status at all, so why forbid it? Deer meat looks like calf meat. The suspect could sell real בכור calf meat and call it deer.

keyTerms.meaning: it gets mixed up or confused

phrases.english: GEMARA: Deer meat?
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה from step 5, which said you may not buy even deer meat from the suspect.

phrases.english: Because it is confused with calf meat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Deer meat looks like calf meat, so a בכור calf could be passed off as deer.

steps.title: Inference that tanned hides may be bought
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's ban on untanned hides, the גמרא infers that tanned hides may be bought.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Nor hides that are not tanned.' This implies that tanned hides we may buy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה and reads a hidden rule out of it. This sets up the next step, which explains the reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only banned untanned hides. That limit suggests tanned hides are allowed. The reason comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: this implies; the flip side is

phrases.english: 'Nor hides that are not tanned.'
This implies that tanned ones we may buy.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Tanned hides may be bought from the suspect.

steps.title: Why tanned hides are trusted
steps.stepSummary: A suspect would not bother tanning a בכור hide, because he would fear the חכמים would take it away from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were from a בכור, he would not bother working on it. He would think: if the רבנן hear about it, they will make me lose it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why a tanned hide can be trusted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Tanning takes work and money. A man who knows the hide is from a בכור is afraid the חכמים might find out and take it. So he would not put effort into it. That is why a tanned hide is presumed not to be from a בכור.

phrases.english: If it were really from a firstborn,
he would not have bothered with it,
thinking: if the Sages hear about it,
they will make me lose it.
phrases.notes: He means the חכמים would take the hide away, and all his tanning work would be wasted.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם אִיתָא דִּבְכוֹר הֲוָה לָא הֲוָה טָרַח בֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for the inference in step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: No one invests in tanning a hide he could lose, so a tanned hide is presumed not to be from a בכור.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows a common idea: we can trust a person when his own interests point the other way.

steps.title: Asking the reason for רבי אליעזר's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר, who allows buying female hides, and asks for his reason.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר says: we may buy hides of female animals from him. What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings back רבי אליעזר's view from the משנה and asks why he is not worried.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A female animal can never be a בכור. Still, the question is how the buyer can be sure the hide is really female.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer says:
We may buy hides of female animals from him.
What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה: רבי אליעזר's view from step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבי אליעזר trusts that a hide sold as female is really female.

steps.title: A female hide is easy to recognize
steps.stepSummary: People can tell whether a hide came from a male or a female animal.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is clearly known.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that a female hide is easy to recognize.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The skin of a male and a female animal look different because of their bodies. So the suspect cannot pass off a male בכור hide as a female one.

keyTerms.meaning: it is clearly known, easy to recognize

phrases.english: It is clearly known.
phrases.notes: He means you can tell from the hide itself whether the animal was male or female.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A male hide and a female hide look different, so a female hide can be recognized.

steps.title: Why does the תנא קמא disagree
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא קמא forbids female hides if they are easy to recognize.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the תנא קמא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the other side: if female hides are easy to identify, why does the תנא קמא still forbid them? This sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given for רבי אליעזר seems strong. So the תנא קמא must have some worry that this reason does not solve.

keyTerms.meaning: the first opinion stated in the משנה

phrases.english: And the first tanna?
phrases.notes: The word 'why does he forbid it?' is understood here, even though it is not written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the reason from step 12 into a question on the other opinion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the תנא קמא is worried about, given that female hides can be recognized.

steps.title: The תנא קמא fears a trick: blaming mice
steps.stepSummary: The seller might cut off the male part of a בכור hide and claim mice ate it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, he will also cut away the male organ of a male hide and say, 'Mice ate it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the תנא קמא's worry: a trick that would make a male hide look female.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If we allow female hides, the seller could cut away the part of the skin that shows the animal was male. Then he would explain the missing piece by saying mice chewed it. So the easy sign is no longer reliable.

phrases.english: If so, a male one too
he will cut away its male organ
and say, 'Mice ate it.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, זָכָר נָמֵי חָיֵיק לְזַכְרוּתֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The sign can be faked by cutting off the male part and blaming mice.

steps.title: Why is רבי אליעזר not worried about the trick
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי אליעזר deals with the 'mice ate it' trick.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now asks רבי אליעזר's side: why isn't he afraid of this trick? This sets up his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא's worry sounds real. So רבי אליעזר needs some reason to reject it.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: This means רבי אליעזר. The question is why he is not worried about the mice trick.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the תנא קמא's worry into a question on רבי אליעזר.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How רבי אליעזר answers the fear that the male part was cut off and blamed on mice.

steps.title: Mouse damage can be recognized
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר holds that you can tell mouse damage from a knife cut, so the trick would not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: The place where mice ate is clearly recognizable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers for רבי אליעזר: a spot chewed by mice looks different from a spot cut with a knife.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Mice leave chewed, rough edges, while a knife leaves a clean cut. So if a seller cut away the male part, people would notice. That is why רבי אליעזר still allows female hides.
steps.whatToRemember: Both sides agree a female hide can be recognized. They argue only about whether a seller can hide a cut: the תנא קמא fears the 'mice ate it' excuse, and רבי אליעזר says mouse damage is easy to spot.

phrases.english: The place of the mice is clearly known.
phrases.notes: He means you can see whether a piece was chewed by mice or cut off with a knife.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 and closes the disagreement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Mouse damage looks different from a knife cut, so the trick would be noticed.

steps.title: Why mention dirty wool after bleached wool?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ban on buying bleached and dirty wool and asks why dirty wool needs to be mentioned at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: We may not buy bleached or dirty wool from him. Now, if we may not even buy bleached wool, do we really need to be told about dirty wool?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line of the משנה about a person suspected with בכור and challenges its wording. If even bleached wool is forbidden, dirty wool is obviously forbidden, so why list both?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Bleached wool has had more work put into it, so you might have thought it was safer to buy. If the משנה forbids even that, dirty raw wool is clearly forbidden. Listing both looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, since (opens a 'this is obvious' challenge)
Is it needed? (do we need to be told?)

phrases.english: And we do not buy from him
phrases.notes: 'Him' is the person suspected about בכור animals, from the start of this משנה.

phrases.english: bleached wool or dirty wool.
Now, if bleached wool we may not buy,
is dirty wool even needed to be said?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַשְׁתָּא צֶמֶר מְלוּבָּן לָא זָבְנִינַן, צוֹאִי מִיבַּעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה after finishing the discussion of hides.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of both bleached and dirty wool
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the more processed case is forbidden, the less processed case is obvious and should not need mentioning.

steps.title: It is one case: wool cleaned of its dirt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה is not listing two cases. It describes one kind of wool: wool that has been bleached clean of its dirt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the משנה is teaching one case: wool that has been bleached clean from its dirt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by reading the two words as one description. The משנה means wool that was washed and whitened from its dirt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed 'bleached' and 'dirty' were two separate items. The answer joins them: the 'dirty' part tells us what the wool was cleaned from. So nothing in the משנה is extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (brings in a new way of reading)

phrases.english: Rather, it is teaching one case:
wool bleached clean from its dirt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 17.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the wording: two words describe one case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Bleached and dirty wool were two separate items, making one of them extra.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is one item: wool cleaned of its dirt, and that is forbidden.

steps.title: Why mention garments after spun thread?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes that spun thread and garments may be bought, and asks why garments need to be mentioned.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: But we may buy spun thread and garments from him. Now, if we may buy spun thread, do we really need to be told about garments?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and asks the same kind of question. If spun thread is allowed, garments made from it are surely allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Spun thread is allowed because so much work has gone into it that we assume it is not from a בכור. Garments have even more work in them, so allowing them seems obvious.

phrases.english: But we may buy from him
spun thread and garments.
Now, if spun thread we may buy,
are garments even needed to be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same kind of challenge as step 17, now on the next line of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of garments after spun thread
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the less finished item is allowed, the more finished item is obviously allowed.

steps.title: Garments here means felt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'garments' means felt items, which are made without spinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'garments' mean? Felt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'garments' refers to felt, which is pressed wool and never spun into thread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Felt skips the spinning step, so you might have thought it is not processed enough to be safe. The משנה teaches that felt garments may still be bought. So the word is not extra.

phrases.english: What are 'garments'?
Felt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 19.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining a term to make it a new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Garments are made from spun thread, so mentioning them adds nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Garments means felt, which is not spun, and the משנה teaches it may still be bought.

steps.title: New משנה: the person suspected about שביעית
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה rules that we may not buy flax, even combed flax, from someone suspected about שביעית, but we may buy spun and woven goods.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: From someone suspected of breaking the laws of שביעית, we may not buy flax, not even combed flax. But we may buy spun thread and woven cloth from them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts. It applies the same idea to a person suspected of breaking the laws of שביעית: raw flax is forbidden, but spun and woven goods are allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even combed flax, which has had work done to it, is still forbidden. Once the flax has been spun or woven, buying it is allowed. This matches the pattern of the wool rules in the earlier משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: One suspected of breaking the laws of the seventh year

steps.whatToRemember: Raw or partly worked material is forbidden from a suspected person; spun or woven goods are allowed.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who is suspected about the seventh year
we may not buy flax from him,
and not even combed flax,
but we may buy spun and woven goods from them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that applies the same pattern to a different suspicion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From one suspected about שביעית, flax (even combed) may not be bought; spun and woven goods may be bought.

steps.title: Why mention woven goods after spun thread?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה mentions woven goods if spun thread is already allowed.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: Now, if we may buy spun thread, do we really need to be told about woven goods?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the same question it asked about garments. If spun thread is allowed, woven cloth made from it is surely allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Woven cloth has had even more work put into it than spun thread. So listing it seems to add nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: גמרא (start of the discussion on the new משנה)

phrases.english: GEMARA: Now, if spun thread we may buy,
is woven cloth even needed to be said?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the same challenge as step 19, now on the new משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's listing of woven goods after spun thread
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If spun thread is allowed, woven cloth, which has even more work in it, is obviously allowed.

steps.title: Woven here means braided chains
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that 'woven' means braided chains, which are made without spinning.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'woven' mean? Braided chains.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that 'woven' means braided chains, which are not made from spun thread. This mirrors the felt answer in step 20.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since these chains skip spinning, you might have thought they count like raw material. The משנה teaches they may still be bought, so the word is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Braided chains or cords, made without spinning

steps.whatToRemember: Each time, the second word of the משנה turns out to mean an item made without spinning: felt for wool, braided chains for flax.

phrases.english: What is 'woven'?
Braided chains.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 22.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defining a term to make it a new case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Woven means cloth made from spun thread, so mentioning it adds nothing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Woven means braided chains that are not spun, and they may still be bought.

steps.title: New משנה: buying from someone suspected about תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה brings a dispute. רבי יהודה forbids buying even water and salt from someone suspected of selling תרומה as חולין. רבי שמעון forbids only items that תרומה and מעשרות can apply to.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If a person is suspected of selling תרומה as ordinary food, we may not buy from him even water and salt. These are the words of רבי יהודה. רבי שמעון says: anything connected to תרומה and מעשרות may not be bought from him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens a new topic. It brings a dispute about what we may buy from a seller suspected of passing off תרומה as ordinary food.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה is very strict: he forbids even water and salt, which can never become תרומה. רבי שמעון ties the ban to the item itself, so only things that תרומה and מעשרות can apply to are forbidden. That leaves water and salt allowed in his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Someone under suspicion of breaking a law
The portion of produce given to a כהן; a non-כהן may not eat it
A connection or link to something

steps.confusionAlert: The two opinions are not arguing about whether the seller can be trusted. Both agree he is suspect. They argue only about which items the suspicion covers.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who is suspected of selling teruma
as if it were ordinary food
we may not buy from him
even water and salt,
these are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.
Rabbi Shimon says:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ זִיקַּת תְּרוּמָה וּמַעַשְׂרוֹת
phrases.english: anything that has a connection to teruma and tithes
we may not buy from him.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִי׳ הֶחָשׁוּד לִהְיוֹת מוֹכֵר תְּרוּמָה לְשׁוּם חוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the earlier משנה about someone suspected regarding שביעית to a parallel case of someone suspected regarding תרומה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהודה: buy nothing, even water and salt, from one suspected of selling תרומה as חולין. רבי שמעון: avoid only items connected to תרומה and מעשרות.

steps.title: What does רבי שמעון's wording add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case is included by רבי שמעון's broad phrase 'anything connected to תרומה and מעשרות.'
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does this come to include?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what extra case רבי שמעון's general phrase is meant to include. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plain produce is obviously connected to תרומה, so it seems clear it is forbidden. The broad wording 'anything that has a connection' suggests רבי שמעון means to include something less obvious. The גמרא wants to know what that is.

keyTerms.meaning: 'To include what?' The גמרא asks what extra case a phrase adds

phrases.english: GEMARA:
What does it come to include?
phrases.notes: This is about רבי שמעון's words 'anything that has a connection to תרומה and מעשרות.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks closely at the wording of רבי שמעון's opinion in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which non-obvious item is included by the phrase 'anything that has a connection to תרומה and מעשרות.'

steps.title: It includes fish innards mixed with olive oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי שמעון's wording includes fish innards, because people mix olive oil into them, and that oil might be תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It comes to include fish innards, because people mix olive oil into them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: רבי שמעון's phrase includes fish innards.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Fish are not produce, so תרומה does not apply to the fish itself. But olive oil is commonly mixed into the innards, and that oil could be תרומה oil. So the dish has a 'connection' to תרומה through what is added to it, and we may not buy it from the suspect.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבי שמעון, an item is forbidden from the suspect even if תרומה does not apply to it directly, as long as something commonly mixed into it, like olive oil, could be תרומה.

phrases.english: It comes to include fish innards,
since people mix olive oil into them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of what רבי שמעון's wording includes.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The phrase includes fish innards, because olive oil, which may be תרומה, is mixed into them.

steps.title: A story begins about a suspected butcher
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts telling a story about a butcher who was suspected of selling something. The story continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a certain butcher who was suspected of selling...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new story about a butcher under suspicion. This line only sets up the story, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After discussing which items we may buy from suspected sellers, the גמרא now brings a real-life case. We are not yet told what the butcher was suspected of selling or what was ruled. Those details come next.

keyTerms.meaning: A certain (person); a common way to start a story

phrases.english: There was a certain butcher
who was suspected of selling

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the משנה's general rules about suspected sellers to a real case of a suspected butcher.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a story about a butcher who was suspected of selling something; what he sold and the ruling come on the next amud.
